The petitioners filed the petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 for seeking compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- with interest and costs of the petition, for the death of Mr.Sandeep caused in road traffic accident.

02. The facts in brief of the petitioner's case is that, on 16.07.2012 at about 1.30 to 2.00 a.m. when the deceased was proceeding in bicycle along with his brother on Hosur - Bengaluru NH-7 Service road, Anekal taluk and when they reached Opp. S.K.F. Factory, at that time, the driver of the Tata Sumo bearing Reg. No.KA-05-AA-7985 by driving it in a rash and negligent manner with high speed, dashed against the bicycle of the deceased from behind, as a result, he fell down and sustained injuries and succumbed to the injuries on the same day.
It is contended that, the deceased Sandeep was aged about 18 years and he was doing tea business and earning Rs.250/- to 300/- per day.

It is also contended that, he was contributing his entire Meenakshmamma vs Sanjeev Reddy on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145359443/
2 income for the welfare and maintenance of petitioner's family.

Due to untimely demise of Sandeep,
the said petitioners who are claiming to be his mother, sister and brother have lost their only bread earning member and his love and affection.
Hence, they SCCH 8 4 MVC No.6127/2012 filed the present claim petition seeking compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- together with interest and costs of the claim petition from respondents.
03. Inspite of service of summons, the 1 st respondent remained absent hence, he was placed exparte.
The 2 nd respondent appeared through its counsel and filed written statement.
04. The respondent No.2 has appeared before the court and filed written statement and denied the entire petition averments.
It has admitted the issuance of policy in respect of the offending vehicle and the liability if any is subject to the terms and conditions of the policy and provisions of the motor vehicles Act.
The driver of the vehicle had no valid and effective driving license and he did not possess driving license.

It is also contended that, the 1st respondent has failed to comply with the mandatory provisions of Sec.134(c) of the MV Act and even the jurisdictional police have also failed to comply with the mandatory provisions of Sec.158(6) of the MV Act.
On these grounds, the 2nd respondent has prayed for dismissing the claim petition with costs.

On the basis of above pleadings the issues have been framed by my predecessor in office are recasted as follows;
1) Whether the petitioners prove that they are the legal heirs of deceased Sandeep?
2) Whether the petitioners proves that on 16.07.2012 at about 1.30 to 2.00 a.m. when the deceased was proceeding in bicycle along with his brother on Hosur - Bengaluru NH-7 Service road, Anekal taluk and when they reached Opp. S.K.F. Factory, at that time, the driver of the Tata Sumo bearing Reg. No.KA-05-AA-7985 by driving it in a rash and negligent manner with high speed, dashed against the bicycle of the deceased from behind, as a result, he fell down and sustained injuries and succumbed to the injuries on the same day as alleged by the petitioners?
3) Whether the petitioners are entitled for any compensation?
If so to what extent and from whom?

4) What Order or Award?
06.

In order to prove the case of the petitioners, the 1st petitioner got examined herself as PW.1 and produced 15 documents which were marked as Ex.P1 to 15 and 3 rd petitioner was examined as PW.2.
SCCH 8 6 MVC No.6127/2012 07.
On the other hand, respondents have not led their defence evidence.

3 08.
Heard the arguments.
The petitioners in order to prove that they are the legal heirs have produced the notarized copies of school record and Aadhaar cards which are marked at Ex.P11 to 15.

On perusal of these documents,
it goes to show that petitioners No.1 to 3 are mother, sister and brother of the deceased Sandeep.
Hence, they are the legal heirs of the deceased.
Therefore, I answered Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
11. Issue No.2:

The petitioners in order to prove the petition averments examined the 1st petitioner as PW1, she deposed that the deceased Sandeep was her son who SCCH 8 7 MVC No.6127/2012 succumbed due to the injuries sustained in the road traffic accident that occurred on 16.07.2012 when the deceased was proceeding in the bicycle along with his brother, on Hosur - Bengaluru NH-7 Service road, Anekal taluk and when they reached Opp. S.K.F. Factory, at that time, the driver of the Tata Sumo bearing Reg. No.KA-05-AA-7985 by driving it in a rash and negligent manner with high speed, dashed against the bicycle of the deceased from behind, as a result, he fell down and sustained injuries and succumbed to the injuries on the same day.
12.
In order to prove the oral evidence petitioner No.1 has produced 15 documents which were marked as Ex.
P1 to P15

. Ex.1 is the F.I.R, Ex.P2 is the true copy of complaint, Ex.P3 is the statement given by the 3 rd petitioner before the police, Ex.P4 is the true copy of spot Mahazar, Ex.P5 is the sketch, Ex.P6 is the true copy of Vehicle seizure mahazar, Ex.P7 is the true copy of IMV Report,
Ex.P8 is the true copy of Inquest report, Ex.P9 is the PM report, Ex.P10 is the charge sheet, Ex.P11 is the school admission record of deceased, Ex.P12 to 15 are the notarized copy of ration cards.
13. On appreciation of evidence of PW.1, she is not an eye witness to the alleged accident.

In her examination SCCH 8 8 MVC No.6127/2012 she deposed that the driver of the car drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the bicycle and as such, her son fell down and sustained injuries and succumbed to death due to injuries.
The first informant is also not an eye witness to the alleged accident and based on the information received by him from the eye witnesses he gave first information.
The alleged accident was taken place on 16.07.2012 and first information was given on 09.00 a.m. i.e. on the same day.
There is no delay in loding the first information.
The evidence of PW.1 is in noway helpful to the petitioners to prove the alleged accident.
Based on the information received by her, and based o n the police documents she deposed that the alleged accident was taken place on 16.07.2012.

Meenakshmamma vs Sanjeev Reddy on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145359443/
4 14.
The 3rd petitioner is examined before the court as PW.2.
He is the brother of deceased.
On the date of accident the 3rd petitioner was proceeding in bicycle along with deceased.

He deposed before the court that when they were proceeding on Bengaluru-Hosur NH-7 service road and when they reached near SKF factory, the driver of the car bearing Reg. No.KA-05-AA-7985 being driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against their bicycle from behind, and as a result they fell down and his brother sustained injuries.
He further deposed during the course of cross examination that he had not lost SCCH 8 9 MVC No.6127/2012 conscious and he saw the vehicle which caused the accident.
This witness gave statement before the police on the date of accident itself wherein also he clearly stated that the driver of the tata sumo dashed against their bicycle from behind.
The evidence of this witness is not shaken by the learned counsel for respondent No.2 during the course of cross examination.
15. In order to substantiate the oral evidence of PW.3, the PW.1 produced the mahazar and sketch marked as Ex.P4 and 5.
The width of the service road is approximately 80 feet and alleged accident was taken place on the eastern side of the road.
The deceased proceeding in his bicycle on his extreme left side.
The driver of the car inspite of sufficient space on his right side, hit against the bicycle from behind.
If the driver drove his TATA Sumo sumo in a slow manner, at least he could have applied the brake and avoided the accident.
Since he was driving the TATA Sumo in a rash manner, he was unable to control and apply the brake and hit against the bicycle, as such, Sandeep died in the hospital on the same day.

The learned counsel for respondent made an effort during the course of cross examination to disprove the say of the PW.2 and in that effort he put a suggestion that there are no other vehicles plying on the road at the time of the accident for which the PW.2 admitted the suggestion.
It is also SCCH 8 10 MVC No.6127/2012 admitted that there are street lights at the place of accident, for which the witness deposed that there are many street lights at the place of accident.
These suggestions helpful to the petitioners.
The road is vacant and there were no vehicles plying on the road except the offending vehicle and the bicycle and because of street lights one can see the other.
Inspite of it, the driver of the tata sumo hit against the bicycle from behind.

Even though he saw the bicycle and even there was sufficient space on his right side. Hence, in the opinion of this tribunal, the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the car by its driver.
16. The I.O filed charge sheet after conclusion of investigation against the driver of the tata sumo which is not disputed.
The IMV report discloses that there is no mechanical defect in the vehicle.
The PM report marked as Ex.P9 discloses that Sandeed died in road traffic accident.

The deceased and petitioners are permanent residents of Sorekunte of Sira taluk, Tumkur district and as such,
they have no enmity against the driver of the car to lodge false first information and they have no friendship with the IO to file false charge sheet through him against the driver of the TATA Sumo.

The documents placed before the tribunal coupled with oral evidence establishes that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of SCCH 8 11 MVC No.6127/2012 the offending TATA Sumo bearing Registration No.KA-05- AA-7985 and deceased succumbed to the injuries in the said accident.
Hence I answered Issue No.2 in the Affirmative.
17. Issue No.3:
According to the petitioners the age of the deceased Sandeep at the time of accident was 18 years.

The petitioners in order to prove the same produced the notarized copy of the school Meenakshmamma vs Sanjeev Reddy on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145359443/
5 record and adhaar card which are marked as Ex.P11 and 15 respectively wherein the date of birth of deceased is shown as 12.04.1997 and the accident was occurred on 16.07.2012.
Hence on the date of accident the age of deceased was 15 years.
The Postmortem report, inquest, Charge sheet reveals that the cause of death of deceased is due to injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.
Hence the petitioner's being the legal heirs are entitle for compensation.
18. Loss of Dependency : The age of the deceased on the date of accident was 15 years.
According to the petitioners the deceased Sandeep was self employed and doing tea business and earning Rs.250/- to 300/- per day.
But they have not produced any documents to show that he was earning Rs.250/- to 300/-.
As stated above the age of deceased Sandeep at the time of accident was 15 years.

The petitioners No.1 and 2 were depending on the income of the deceased and the 3 rd petitioner depend on the deceased to sell the tea, and hence the income of the 3rd petitioner reduces in the absence of deceased.
The father of deceased was predeceased him.
Hence, the petitioners are the dependents.

20. The 3rd petitioner gave statement to the police marked as Ex.P3 goes to show that himself and his deceased brother were proceeding in a bicycle on the date of accident in the midnight in order to sell the tea.
Hence, the say of PW.2 cannot be rejected.
The say of PW.2 is not an after thought.
The came to Bengaluru in order to do business and earn money.

Even though the deceased was minor,
he was earning by selling tea to the labourers of the factory and as such, they were proceeding in bicycle in highway and alleged accident was taken place in front of the factory.
All these circumstances establishes that the deceased was earning money by selling tea.
Hence, even though there is no proof regarding his income, his income is taken as Rs.200/- per day and income per month is construed as Rs.6,000/-.
Hence by applying the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarala Varma Vs DTC reported in AIR 2009 Supreme Court 3104.

entities.text: Sarala Varma Vs DTC reported in AIR 2009 Supreme Court 3104
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The deceased was bachelor, hence 50% of income is deducted towards personal and living expenses.
Accordingly, the expenditure of deceased became 1/2 th x 3,000 = 3,000/- and income of deceased per month became 3,000/- (6,000-3,000).
The age of the deceased is 15 years and hence Rs.1,200/- (3,000 x 40%) is added towards future prospectus.

Hence the income of deceased became Rs.4,200/- p.m.
22.
The age of the deceased was 15 years at the time of accident.
Hence, the proper multiplier as per the above citation is 18.

Accordingly, the petitioners are entitle for Rs.4,200 x 12 x 18 = 9,07,200/-
under the head of loss of dependency.
23. Love and affection & filial consortium:
The petitioners being the mother, sister and brother of deceased have lost love and affection of deceased towards them and vice versa.
No amount of compensation gives back the deceased.

Hence by considering all these the petitioners are entitled for Meenakshmamma vs Sanjeev Reddy on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145359443/
6 Rs.1,00,000/- under this head.
24.
Funeral Expenses:

The petitioners in their petition have stated that they have spent Rs.25,000/-
towards funeral expenditure.
In order to prove the same they have not produced any documents.
Hence the SCCH 8 14 MVC No.6127/2012 petitioners are entitled for Rs.10,000/- towards funeral expenditure.
25. Conveyance charges:
The petitioners have not produced any documents to show that they have spent amount towards conveyance.
At the time of incident nobody received the receipt.

The petitioners were residents of Tumkur district and after the Post Mortem the body was taken to their native place by hiring the vehicle and they unable to receive the receipt because of their condition.

Hence by considering these facts the petitioners are entitled for Rs.5,000/-.
26.

The above amount is summarized as follows;
 A) Loss of Estate 09,07,200-00  B) Love and Affection  and filial consortium 1,00,000-00  C) Funeral Expenses 10,000-00  D) Conveyance 5,000-00  Total 10,22,200-00  27.

Hence the petitioners are entitled for Rs.
Rs.10,22,200/- as compensation from respondent No.2.
The respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offended vehicle is liable to indemnify.
The petitioners filed the petition and the same was dismissed for non-prosecution.

Thereafter,
the petitioner filed the miscellaneous petition and in the said petition they have stated that they will give up the interest.
The said miscellaneous petition was filed in the year 2023 and petition was dismissed on 23.06.2014.
The learned counsel for petitioner submits that the petitioners are entitled for interest from the date of petition till dismissal of the petition.
The petitioners have not led evidence till 06.11.2023.

Hence, the petitioners are not entitled for interest from the date of petition,
but they are entitled for interest from the date of evidence i.e. from 06.11.2023 at the rate of 6% till the amount deposited by the respondent No.2.
Accordingly I answered issue No.3 partly in the affirmative.
29. Issue No.4:
In view of the foregoing reasons I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER The petition filed by the petitioners u/s 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is partly allowed with cost.

Meenakshmamma vs Sanjeev Reddy on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145359443/
7

The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.10,22,200/-(Rupees Ten SCCH 8 16 MVC No.6127/2012 lakhs Twenty two thousand two hundred only) along with interest at the rate of 6% from 06.11.2023 till the date of realization.
The respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation amount.
Further the respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the above said amount within 2 months from the date of this order along with accrued interest.
After deposit made by the respondent No.2, the petitioner No.1 is entitled to receive 50% and petitioners No.2 and 3 are entitled for 25% each from compensation amount.

The matter is of the year 2012 and as such the petitioners are entitled to receive the entire amount of compensation as per their share through e-payment after verification of adhaar card and passbook.

Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-
Draw Award accordingly.
